task.title: Conditional rules
task.shortdesc: A conditional rule contains rules that participate in the cascade only when its condition is true. A condition filters rules; it does not give declarations extra priority. Declarations that pass the condition compete by the usual cascade order.

info.p: CSS Conditional 3 §5, Media-specific style sheets: the @media rule; Media Queries 5 §2, Media Queries.

@media tests a media query list. Queries can test a media type, media features, or both. A comma separates alternatives: the list matches if at least one query is true. and combines a media type or feature with another test. not negates the complete query. only has no effect on whether a query matches.

CSSMedia evaluates media types for paged output. print and all match. screen does not. A query without a media type is treated as all. Media feature queries are evaluated against the page and environment values CSSMedia uses.
CSS Conditional 3 §6, Feature queries: the @supports rule; CSS Conditional 5 §2, Extensions to the @supports rule.
@supports tests whether CSSMedia accepts a declaration or selector. A declaration test uses parentheses:

Use selector() to test one complex selector. CSS also defines font-tech() and font-format() tests. at-rule() tests whether an at-rule is supported, and a named support condition can test a group declared with @supports-condition. Conditions can combine tests with not, and and or; use parentheses when combining and and or.
A true feature test means the tested syntax is accepted. It does not test whether a selector matches any element or whether a particular document contains a value.
CSS Conditional 5 §8, Defining Custom Support Queries: the @supports-condition rule.

@supports-condition gives a name to a group of feature tests. Declarations and nested selectors in the block are tested for support; they do not add styling declarations. Define the name before using it:
If more than one definition uses the same name, the last definition in document order replaces the earlier one.
CSS Conditional 5 §3, Generalized Conditional Rules: the @when rule.
@when tests a boolean condition that can combine media() and supports() tests. It provides a single condition syntax for tests that would otherwise appear in separate @media or @supports rules.
Conditions can be grouped with parentheses and combined with and, or and not.
CSS Conditional 5 §4, Chained Conditionals: the @else rule.

An @else rule follows an @when, @media, @supports or @container rule to form a chain. Only the first branch whose condition is true applies. @else can have its own condition; without one, it is the final fallback.
Each @else belongs to the immediately preceding conditional chain in the same rule list. An unrelated rule or declaration ends the chain.
Media Queries 5 §10, Custom Media Queries.
@custom-media assigns a name to a media query list, or to the boolean value true or false. Use the name in a media query by writing it inside parentheses:
A definition can refer to other custom media names. Circular references do not produce a true query. When a name is defined more than once, the last definition is used.
CSS Conditional 5 §5.1, Creating Query Containers: the container-type property; §5.4, Container Queries: the @container rule.

@container selects a query container from the element’s ancestors. A container name before the condition restricts which ancestor is selected. A style query tests a computed style or custom property on the selected container. Conditions can combine tests with and, or and not.

A style query can use an element as a container without size containment. Without a name, the nearest eligible ancestor is used. With a name, the nearest ancestor whose container-name includes that name is used.
CSS Cascade 5 §2, Importing Style Sheets: the @import rule; CSS Cascade 5 §2.1, Conditional @import Rules.

@import loads another stylesheet. Its rules take part in the cascade at the import’s position. The URL or quoted string comes first. Optional clauses can assign the imported rules to a layer, test feature support, or restrict them to matching media:

An optional @charset, layer-order statements and @supports-condition rules can precede imports. Imports precede @namespace; namespace declarations precede ordinary rules. An import after another rule is ignored. Imports can be conditional. If an import condition is false, its rules do not participate. A layer clause places the imported stylesheet in that layer; an unnamed layer creates an anonymous layer.
CSS Cascade 5 §6.4, Cascade Layers.
@layer declares a layer order or groups rules into a layer:

Declarations in layers use the layer precedence described in Cascade order and layers. Layer statements establish order, and layer blocks group rules. An @import can assign its imported rules to a layer with a layer clause.
CSS Namespaces 3 §3.1, Syntax.

@namespace declares prefixes used by selectors. See Basic selectors and namespaces. Conditional rules and imports can also contain @page rules; page declarations use the page-context cascade described in Cascade order and layers.
